why: I checked every verifier PASS/FAIL condition against its expect line. None is stricter than its line. Check 1 asks only that each output line starts with `$T/bad.jsonl:3: ` or `$T/bad.jsonl:6: ` and has "a non-empty error text", so no exact wording is required. Check 2 only needs stderr to be non-empty and exit code 2. Check 4 allows `node --test` with "extra flags/paths after it". Check 6 asks for exactly one PR and the Closes text, both of which the line itself names. There is no branch-name rule, no mutation test and no limit on which files the PR may touch. The shebang, CRLF and lock-file checks sit under "Advisory" and are marked "do not fail". The behaviour lines (1–3) are checked by running the CLI and calling lint() on real input, not by reading the diff. Check 4 runs the tests and also reads the test files, which suits a line about which tests exist. The builder brief adds no file restrictions.
